sentences.zh: 今年我一直在以一种切合实际的方式优先关注自己的健康，而让我保持动力的东西就是我的WHOOP。

sentences.zh: WHOOP能轻松追踪我的睡眠、体能消耗、恢复情况、压力，以及最最重要的整体健康状况。

sentences.en: And it just gives me all that data and all those patterns so I can make better decisions, which includes knowing when to go easy and knowing when to go hard.
sentences.zh: 它只是给我提供所有这些数据和模式，以便我能做出更好的决定，包括知道什么时候该轻松应对，什么时候该全力以赴。

sentences.zh: 萨姆探讨了那些构成我们一部分的记忆、执念和微小珍宝。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《The Psychology of Your 20s》，这是一个探讨我们在二十岁时所经历的一些重大生活改变与过渡，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及这些改变对我们的心理意味着什么的播客。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身处世界的哪个角落，很高兴你能回来收听又一期节目。

sentences.en: Today, we are talking about a much-requested topic and one that I think is highly personally relevant to me, understanding and overcoming our social anxiety.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要探讨一个呼声很高的话题，而且我认为它与我个人息息相关——理解并克服我们的社交焦虑。

sentences.en: When we think about our 20s, there are a few generally universal experiences I think we can all agree on and worrying about the opinions of others being very self-critical,
sentences.zh: 当我们回想自己的二十岁时，有一些普遍共有的经历是我们都会认同的，比如担心别人的看法、极度自我批判，

sentences.en: concerned about whether we've embarrassed ourselves, our past mistakes, the times we've overshared or said the wrong thing.
sentences.zh: 担心自己是否出丑、过去的错误，以及那些分享过头或说错话的时刻。

sentences.en: That is definitely one of them.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是其中之一。

sentences.en: It's definitely a common thing that haunts us and keeps us up at night.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一种困扰着我们、让我们夜不能寐的常见现象。

sentences.en: There are so many experiences like this that I think live in our head rent-free, taking up the space that we perhaps could be using for other things,
sentences.zh: 有太多这样的经历，我认为它们不请自来地占据着我们的脑海，霸占了我们本来可以用来做其他事情的空间，

sentences.en: but also causing us to avoid certain situations or events out of fear of that really physical and emotional, even mental discomfort.
sentences.zh: 同时也让我们因为害怕那种真实的身体、情感甚至精神上的不适，而选择逃避某些情况或活动。

sentences.en: And it can be really hard to wrangle with those thoughts and wrangle with that anxiety and bring it back into our control.
sentences.zh: 要与这些想法和焦虑作斗争并将其重新掌控在自己手中，确实非常困难。

sentences.en: This is particularly the case because as we know, our brains are hardwired to seek the approval and the safety of others.
sentences.zh: 之所以尤其如此，是因为正如我们所知，我们的大脑天生就会寻求他人的认可与安全感。

sentences.en: So when we think that perhaps we've done something that is wrong or we've done something that could be seen as awkward or cause us to be rejected or perceived negatively,
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们认为自己可能做了错事，或者做了可能被视为尴尬、导致我们被拒绝或产生负面印象的事情时，

sentences.en: our minds automatically set off an alarm system and it triggers a fear response that we come to know as social anxiety.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑就会自动拉响警报系统，触发一种我们所熟知的恐惧反应——社交焦虑。

sentences.en: And people feel this in so many areas of their lives when it comes to making new friends, to dating, job interviews, to lowering their inhibitions in front of new people.
sentences.zh: 人们在生活的诸多方面都会感受到这一点，比如结新朋友、约会、求职面试，以及在生人面前卸下防备。

sentences.en: And I want you to know that you are not alone in that experience.
sentences.zh: 我希望你知道，在经历这种感受时，你并不孤单。

sentences.en: I think any type of anxiety can cause us to feel very solitary and isolated because the only person whose reality we really understand is our own.
sentences.zh: 我认为任何类型的焦虑都会让我们感到非常孤独和孤立，因为我们真正能理解其现实的只有我们自己。

sentences.en: So we tend to be hypercritical and hyperfixated on our interpretation of an event rather than our objective reality, one in which most people
sentences.zh: 所以我们往往会过度批判、过度纠结于自己对某件事的解读，而不是我们的客观现实——在现实中，大多数人

sentences.en: really aren't looking at us that closely.
sentences.zh: 其实并没有那么仔细地看着我们。

sentences.en: We are all very much selfish beings who spend a lot of time ruminating on our faults, wondering who may be thinking about us when no one is because we're all in the same boat.
sentences.zh: 我们本质上都是极其自私的生物，花费大量时间反刍自己的缺点，琢磨是否有人在想我们，其实根本没有人，因为我们都身处同一条船上。

sentences.en: So today I really want to discuss some of the ways that we can control our social anxiety or at least understand it better and make peace with those feelings
sentences.zh: 所以今天我真的很想讨论一些方法，让我们能够控制自己的社交焦虑，或者至少更好地理解它，与这些感受握手言和，

sentences.en: and not let them hold us back from the joy, the excitement, the surprises of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 不要让它们阻碍我们去拥抱二十岁的快乐、兴奋和惊喜。

sentences.en: We are going to examine why we feel socially anxious and what actually is perhaps a deeper social phobia.
sentences.zh: 我们将审视为什么我们会感到社交焦虑，以及什么才可能是更深层的社交恐惧症。

sentences.en: Where does that fear come from?
sentences.zh: 这种恐惧从何而来？

sentences.en: We'll also look at the major cognitive distortions that try and convince us that we are awkward, that we are embarrassing or socially inept and why those distortions are false.
sentences.zh: 我们还将探讨主要的认知扭曲，它们试图说服我们自己很尴尬、很出丑或社交笨拙，并解释为什么这些扭曲是错误的。

sentences.en: There is also such an interesting relationship between overthinking, perfectionism and social anxiety that is rarely discussed and I think it relates to a lot of people
sentences.zh: 过度思考、完美主义和社交焦虑之间还存在着一种非常有趣的关系，这很少被讨论，我认为它与我交谈过的很多人以及我自己的情况都有关。

sentences.en: that I speak to and also my own situation as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我自己的情况也是如此。

sentences.en: So how can we use that understanding, use that broader knowledge of our social anxiety to reclaim our authenticity, to reclaim our confidence
sentences.zh: 那么，我们如何利用这种理解、利用对社交焦虑的更广泛认知来重拾真实的自我，重拾自信，

sentences.en: and not live in that shadow of someone else's opinion or our perception of someone else's opinion of us?
sentences.zh: 而不是活在他人的评价，或是我们对他人如何评价我们的感知之阴影下呢？

sentences.en: There is so much to cover as someone who still remembers
sentences.zh: 作为一个至今仍记得

sentences.en: every embarrassing thing that has happened to me since I was a child, the time I tripped and fell in front of the stairs of someone I really liked
sentences.zh: 自我记事以来发生在我身上的每一件尴尬事的人，比如有一次我在我非常喜欢的人的台阶前绊倒摔倒，

sentences.en: or the time I got really drunk at a work event and said weird things to my boss.
sentences.zh: 或者有一次我在公司活动上喝得大醉，对老板说了些怪话，这里面有太多内容要讲。

sentences.en: I'm here with you but I also have some of the psychology and the hidden explanations and also the advice for why we all feel this way sometimes and why it is not only natural
sentences.zh: 我和你们感同身受，但我也有一些心理学知识、隐藏的解释，以及相关的建议，告诉大家为什么我们有时都会有这种感觉，为什么这不仅很自然，

sentences.en: but something that we can come to learn to control.
sentences.zh: 而且是我们能够学会控制的事情。

sentences.en: So all of that and more, without further ado, let us get into the psychology behind our social anxiety.
sentences.zh: 所有这些以及更多内容，废话不多说，让我们进入社交焦虑背后的心理学。

sentences.en: Every single one of us is going to experience occasional moments of embarrassment, of cringe, of anxiety around social interactions, wondering whether we overshared,
sentences.zh: 我们每一个人都会在社交互动中经历偶尔的尴尬、社死、焦虑时刻，琢磨自己是不是分享得太多了，

sentences.en: whether we said something we don't remember, did that person like me?
sentences.zh: 是不是说了不记得的话，那个人喜欢我吗？

sentences.en: And all of those things are, I think, very common things that I've experienced myself, things that have sometimes really got in the way of me connecting with people deeply
sentences.zh: 所有这些，我认为都是非常常见的现象，我自己也经历过，有时这些事情真的妨碍了我与他人建立深度的连接，

sentences.en: or feeling like I wanted to kind of curl up into a ball and hide away and never speak to anyone ever again.
sentences.zh: 或者让我觉得想缩成一团藏起来，再也不和任何人说话了。

sentences.en: I think that occasional hyper focus on our ability to be perceived and therefore to be judged feels like one that is quite a heavy burden to bear but also one that is felt
sentences.zh: 我认为，偶尔过度关注自己被他人感知并因此被评判的能力，感觉是一种相当沉重的负担，但也是相当一部分人

sentences.en: by quite a few people out there.
sentences.zh: 所共同感受到的。

sentences.en: A part of these experiences and the feelings of being self-conscious or overanalyzing a social situation from time to time is really normal despite it being uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 这些经历的一部分，以及偶尔感到不自在或过度分析社交情境的感觉，其实是非常正常的，尽管它很不舒服。

sentences.en: This reaction is a function of our environment and our evolution and simply put, historically our survival was dependent on group acceptance.
sentences.zh: 这种反应是我们环境和进化的功能，简单来说，从历史上看，我们的生存依赖于群体的接纳。

sentences.en: We needed to be part of the tribe for things like food, shelter and security and if we were outcast, it was essentially a bit of a death sentence.
sentences.zh: 我们需要成为部落的一部分来获取食物、庇护所和安全等资源，如果我们被放逐，基本上就等于判了死刑。

sentences.en: So this necessitated an innate recognition of the opinions and the perspective of the group and also our reputation within it.
sentences.zh: 因此，这就需要天生具备对群体意见和视角以及我们在其中声誉的认知。

sentences.en: So when we act in a way that we think brings attention to us or could put us on the out or garner negativity or rejection,
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们做出自认为会引起注意，或者可能会让我们被排挤、招致负面评价或拒绝的行为时，

sentences.en: what that triggers is a lot of fear or anxiety
sentences.zh: 这所触发的便是大量的恐惧或焦虑，

sentences.en: that is highly instinctual.
sentences.zh: 这种反应是高度本能的。

sentences.en: That uncomfortable feeling, that sense of social anxiety is meant to protect us as annoying as it is.
sentences.zh: 那种不舒服的感觉、那种社交焦虑感，尽管很烦人，但它是为了保护我们而存在的。

sentences.en: It's meant to warn us not to do that again and provide an emotionally salient experience that will keep us in line and that evolutionary instinct that has come
sentences.zh: 它是为了警告我们不要再犯，并提供一种情感上有警示意义的体验，让我们守规矩；而这种进化本能

sentences.en: from a place of survival, it has lingered with us and it continues to create situations and feelings that make us feel uncomfortable, that make us question our worth and question
sentences.zh: 源于生存的需求，它一直挥之不去，并不断制造出让我们感到不舒服、让我们质疑自身价值以及质疑

sentences.en: whether other people like us, what their judgments of us are.
sentences.zh: 别人是否喜欢我们、他们如何评价我们的情境和感受。

sentences.en: There's a really important distinction here though between occasional feelings of being embarrassed or self-conscious and a genuine diagnosable social anxiety disorder,
sentences.zh: 不过，这里有一个非常重要的区别，那就是偶尔感到尴尬或不自在与真正的、可诊断的社交焦虑障碍（

sentences.en: otherwise known as a social phobia.
sentences.zh: 也就是常说的社交恐惧症）之间的区别。

sentences.en: And really the distinction here is based on severity and frequency.
sentences.zh: 这里的区别其实取决于严重程度和频率。

sentences.en: So social anxiety disorder is definitely not uncommon.
sentences.zh: 所以社交焦虑障碍绝对不是什么罕见病。

sentences.en: It's actually the third most common mental health condition behind depression and substance use disorders and the most common form of anxiety.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是仅次于抑郁症和物质使用障碍的第三大常见心理健康问题，也是最常见的焦虑症形式。

sentences.en: So it impacts between I think like 6% to 10% depending on your estimates of people worldwide.
sentences.zh: 因此，据估计它影响了全球大约6%到10%的人口。

sentences.en: And those numbers, those numbers are huge.
sentences.zh: 这些数字，这些数字是极其庞大的。

sentences.en: What this says is that almost 1 in 10 of us are walking around with an intense discomfort and even fear towards social situations.
sentences.zh: 这说明几乎每10个人中就有1个人在日常生活中带着对社交场合的强烈不适甚至恐惧。

sentences.en: And inherent to that is this worry of being judged, of being humiliated, of being outcaSt.
sentences.zh: 而其中固有的是这种被评判、被羞辱、被排挤的担忧。

sentences.en: Because we really do care about the opinions of others even when we try not to.
sentences.zh: 因为我们确实在意他人的看法，哪怕我们极力想要不在乎。

sentences.en: And what this can lead us to do is to avoid certain situations where we might be forced with, you know, forced to interact with people we don't know or maybe, you know,
sentences.zh: 而这可能导致我们去做的一件事，就是逃避某些我们可能会被迫面对的场合，比如被迫与不认识的人互动，或者可能，

sentences.en: situations where we don't know what to say, where we're uncomfortable, unprepared.
sentences.zh: 在那些我们不知该说些什么、感到不适、毫无准备的场合。

sentences.en: Perhaps we kind of have to stand alone in the corner of the party like waiting and awkwardly looking around for someone you know.
sentences.zh: 也许我们不得不孤零零地站在派对的角落里，一边等待，一边尴尬地四处张望寻找认识的人。

sentences.en: Literally the worst feeling ever.
sentences.zh: 这简直是世界上最糟糕的感觉。

sentences.en: But this social anxiety, especially when it's linked to a social anxiety disorder, it causes us to be particularly fearful or anxious towards things like attending parties
sentences.zh: 但这种社交焦虑，尤其是当它与社交焦虑障碍挂钩时，会让我们对参加派对等事情

sentences.en: or social gatherings, going places where we don't know anyone and having to meet new people or start a conversation.
sentences.zh: 或社交聚会、去谁也不认识的地方且必须结识新面孔或发起对话感到格外害怕或焦虑。

sentences.en: Another big one is things like public speaking or speaking up in public settings like in a classroom or during a work presentation and then in more extreme cases.
sentences.zh: 另一个大类是诸如公开演讲，或在课堂或工作汇报等公共场合发言，然后在更极端的情况下，

sentences.en: Some people can have such an intense cognitive and emotional reaction that they struggle doing things like eating or drinking in front of other people or using public spaces
sentences.zh: 有些人可能会产生如此强烈的认知和情感反应，以至于他们甚至难以在别人面前吃东西、喝水，或者使用公共场所

sentences.en: or public restrooMs.
sentences.zh: 或公共洗手间。

sentences.en: The main triggers are situations in which we acknowledge that we can be perceived and that something about our behavior might reveal these parts of us that we are convinced of
sentences.zh: 主要的触发点是这样一些情境：我们意识到自己会被感知，并且我们的某种行为可能会暴露我们确信存在、

sentences.en: but that we are trying to keep invisible.
sentences.zh: 但又极力想掩盖的部分。

sentences.en: Those parts of us that we don't like and we're worried what people will think if they see them.
sentences.zh: 那些我们不喜欢、并担心别人看到后会怎么想的自己。

sentences.en: That we are a fraud, that we are awkward, that we have nothing to say and if people were to find out about this kind of secret side of us we believe it would be
sentences.zh: 担心我们是个骗子、我们很笨拙、我们无话可说，如果人们发现了我们这种秘密的一面，我们相信这将是

sentences.en: the end of the world.
sentences.zh: 世界末日。

sentences.en: We believe that everything around us would come crumbling down and we respond to this possibility with anxiety and anxiety is essentially a fear response particularly
sentences.zh: 我们相信周围的一切都会崩溃，而我们对这种可能性做出的反应就是焦虑，焦虑本质上是一种恐惧反应，尤其是

sentences.en: anticipatory anxiety where we project our fears onto a future situation in anticipation of an event or a situation that might leave us feeling a bit unstable
sentences.zh: 预期性焦虑，即我们在面对可能让我们感到有些不稳定

sentences.en: or a little bit uncertain and the logic the kind of illogic almost goes that if we can anticipate what might go wrong where we might misstep we can put a plan in place
sentences.zh: 或有些不确定的事件或情况时，将恐惧投射到未来的情境中，其逻辑（几乎可以说是毫无逻辑）在于，如果我们能预料到什么可能会出错、我们在哪里可能会失误，我们就能制定一个计划

sentences.en: to be prepared for the worst case scenario and also our brain tells us that the easiest way to minimize the worst case scenario is by avoidance.
sentences.zh: 来为最坏的情况做好准备，而且我们的大脑告诉我们，把最坏情况减到最小的最简单方法就是逃避。

sentences.en: If we actively avoid social situations we don't have to feel anxious and if our goal is to avoid anxiety then that is a very effective way of going about it but it's also
sentences.zh: 如果我们积极逃避社交场合，就不用感到焦虑了；如果我们的目标是逃避焦虑，那这确实是一个非常有效的方法，但遗憾的是，

sentences.en: unfortunately not very sustainable nor is it particularly healthy given that deep social connection and even casual everyday interaction is really vital for maintaining our mood
sentences.zh: 它既不太可持续，也不算特别健康，因为深度的社交连接甚至是日常的随性互动，对于维持我们的情绪

sentences.en: and our well-being.
sentences.zh: 和福祉至关重要。

sentences.en: Also whilst avoidance temporarily makes us feel better it just makes us more fearful in the future because we never give ourselves the opportunity to prove that nasty
sentences.zh: 此外，虽然逃避能让我们暂时感觉好受一些，但它只会让我们在未来变得更加恐惧，因为我们从未给自己提供过机会去证明脑海中那个讨厌的

sentences.en: negative voice in our head wrong.
